title: Junos Monitoring: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Your router is always trying to tell you something. It works like a house alarm. You just have to know where to look.

lines.t: Your router is trying to tell you something

scenes.heading: The house alarm
scenes.narration: The alarm panel has a timeline of everything that happened, even while you were away. The timeline is the log. Each sensor has its own report. Severity runs from zero to seven.

scenes.heading: Checking health
scenes.narration: Three commands cover most checks. Look at the hardware, look at the logs, and reboot only when you must. Check temperature, fans and power. Read the main log. And only then, reboot gracefully.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misunderstandings. For per process detail, use show system processes extensive. There are many logs, each with a purpose. And a graceful reboot is different from a forced one.

items.wrong: show system health shows per-process CPU
messages is the only log that matters
A reboot is always the same

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos monitoring lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Logs live in slash var slash log, and messages is the main one. Show chassis environment checks the hardware. Reboot gracefully, and force only when stuck. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos monitoring lab.

points.t: Logs live in /var/log; messages is main
Graceful reboot; force only when stuck
